input.question: Can someone explain what a mortgage is (LI5)?
input.ground_truth: A mortgage is simply a loan that a bank gives you so that you can buy a house. Most people don't have enough money on hand to pay the full price for a house so they will get a loan from the bank, called a mortgage, that is to be used strictly for the purchase of a house. The bank requires you to pay back a certain amount of the loan, with interest, every month just like any other loan. If you stop paying your mortgage the bank has the legal right to foreclose on your home, which means that they can force you to leave and sell the house to get their money back. Once you pay back your mortgage in full the bank no longer has any legal claim on your house.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you really, really want a big toy castle, but you don’t have enough money right now to buy it. So, you ask your parents (or maybe a bank, which is like a big money helper) if you can pay for the castle a little bit at a time.

Here’s how it works:
- The bank (or your parents) gives you the money to buy the castle right now.
- You promise to give them back that money, but not all at once. Instead, you give them a little bit of money every week or every month.
- You also give them something called "interest," which is like a thank-you gift for helping you.

The promise you make to pay back the money little by little is called a **mortgage**.

So, a mortgage is like borrowing money to buy something big (like a house or a castle), and then paying it back slowly over time.
